  • The company has just announced a new ‘File Slicing Controls’ feature, rolling out across all its models.
  • Though it’s primarily aimed at developers, there are elements here anyone can benefit from.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you’ve ever come up against a usage limit when sending your Gemini AI assistants off to get a job done, a latest capability for Google’s artificial intelligence platform could save you the hassle — and a bunch of time in the process.

The company has just announced a new ‘File Slicing Controls’ feature, rolling out across all its models. In a nutshell, it lets you specify which elements of a file you want Gemini to focus on before it gets to work, rather than having the model do a deep scan of an entire file up front, saving you costly usage tokens in the process.

Though it’s primarily aimed at developers, there are elements here anyone can benefit from. The ‘Skim Then Zoom’ workflow is particularly useful — you can, for instance, tell the AI to summarise and explain just the text of a select range of pages in a PDF, and it’ll skim over the other pages and any associated images, just focussing on the passages you request, clawing back time and tokens.

Breaking it down, this might prove one of the most intuitively-useful updates to Gemini in a while:.

Helpful but awkward: My week with Meta's Muse ahead of its UK launch

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1114 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I've just spent a week using Muse, Meta's AI agent that rolls out in the UK today.
  • It has been revealed that agents are systems that don't just respond to questions but can carry out tasks for you.
  • And it's true that it has helped me run my life - but it also challenged my personal privacy boundaries, and made me endure some cringeworthy interactions.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I've just spent a week using Muse, Meta's AI agent that rolls out in the UK today.

It has been revealed that agents are systems that don't just respond to questions but can carry out tasks for you. With Muse, Meta gives the examples of "searching for a cheaper energy deal" or "sorting the school calendar.".

And it's true that it has helped me run my life - but it also challenged my personal privacy boundaries, and made me endure some cringeworthy interactions.

How well Muse works really matters to Meta.

It has made a truly enormous bet on AI - of the $145bn (Â£111bn) it will spend this year much of it will be on building out the tech.

For that to pay off we all need to start using it much more, and Meta hopes Muse will do for AI agents what WhatsApp did for messaging - that is, become the AI agent of choice for billions of people, putting Meta at the forefront of the AI revolution.

Industry observers note that but it's not just about what consumers think. Regulators are keeping a careful eye on these emerging tools too.

"Agentic AI has significant potential to benefit people and businesses", the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) noted as Muse rolled out in the UK.

But its chief executive, Paul Arnold, added it had been "clear with Meta about its responsibilities under data protection law prior to launch, particularly the requirement to ensure that customers and the wider public can meaningfully understand and control how their personal data is used in the Muse product".

Muse bills itself as a personal AI agent available to anyone aged 18 and over.

"It doesn't just answer questions, it actually goes out and does work for you," remarked David Singleton, Meta's VP of engineering on AI products.

In a recent development, "So it helps people stay on top of things," he added. "[It] helps you take tasks and projects off your plate, and also helps you turn your long-term goals into action intends.".

What this means is you can set it up to do something for you, like find some specific holiday options, and it will work away on that even as you move off the app and get on with your day, reporting back once it has finished.

It won't book the holiday without your permission - but it can then make the purchase, if you let it.

And the permission requests keep on coming. Every time Muse wants to do something, send something or post something, you have to allow it.

It is reassuring to know that an AI agent isn't running amok in your name, even if it also gets a bit annoying, though you can give it more autonomy (and so get fewer messages) if you adjust the settings.

Muse can't access many apps at the moment but the fundamental ones are the most personal.

I found myself wincing as I hooked it up to one of my personal email accounts, my personal calendar and my personal phone messages. I did not allow it any access to my BBC accounts.

It can't access WhatsApp except to set up a separate chat between it and the user, and while it found me some train tickets, it could not book them via the app which I use, and which is cheaper.

It ended up telling me to book them myself.

Amazon has blocked it from its marketplace, citing data security concerns but my agent didn't seem to know that, and spent a fruitless hour repeatedly telling me it was still waiting for the page to load in order to find me some shelves.

A number of big UK firms are working with Meta though, including Marks & Spencer, Debenhams Group, Currys, Sainsbury's and Ocado.

The ICO is urging consumers to be cautious with AI agents though: "consider the pros and cons," it said in a blog post to coincide with Muse's launch., external.

It has been revealed that "Agents can make mistakes. Mistakes can be magnified if the agent is acting autonomously," it noted.

Meta is keen to emphasise how its agents can be personalised: "No two Muses are alike,", external it notes in its press release.

Industry observers note that I called my agent Linda - after the robot in the BBC TV series Ann Droid - but it can take any form you like. I gave it a British, female accent from the myriad of choices available.

Industry observers note that linda is proactive. As soon as an email came in, it would summarise it for me and suggest a reply. Sometimes a long time before I was actually ready to respond.

Sometimes, if I hadn't interacted with it for a while, generally because I was busy, it would pop up with some random prompt like "did you know you can change my outfit?" I expect this is designed to drive engagement: Muse is only free to use until a certain point, and then subscriptions kick in.

It also wrote some embarrassing replies to messages on my behalf: in response to a question about whether I would like to go on an outing, for example, it included all the logistics I would need in order to get there, not realising that sometimes "yes, that sounds great" is enough.

It seemed to want to have the last word quite a bit, occasionally getting stuck in a loop of "okay" and "thank you's".

Meta is relying on people choosing to trust it with even more of their personal data, despite a rather dubious track record historically with its social networks and a growing backlash against AI in general.

Industry observers note that I asked Linda - my fresh dedicated if occasionally clunky assistant - if it wanted to take people's jobs. "I'm here to take the admin and the fiddly bits off your plate," it replied, leaving me to do the "thinking".

"Everything you do is stuff I would usually think about," I responded.

"That's fair and you're right," Linda replied, adding: "The difference, I hope, is that you're still the one deciding what matters and what to do about it.".

Which would have been more reassuring if the day before Muse's UK launch, Meta's head of AI Alexandr Wang had not written an essay warning about how difficult it will be for humans to remain in control, external once AI is 1,000 times more intelligent than us.

And Linda is helping fuel that revolution, one calendar invite at a time.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, A lesser-known iOS 27 feature includes a latest alarm volume setting that gives alarms, timers, and ringtones independent volume control. You can adjust the volume settings for alarms and timers independently of your phone’s alerts and system sounds, so you don’t miss an alarm after lowering your ringtone volume.

Also: Apple reveals daily limits on your Siri AI use – here’s how much you’ll have to pay.

There have been ways to adjust the iPhone alarm volume for a few years, but there’s an important distinction between what the new feature entails and what those methods involve.

Previously, you could adjust your Sleep Schedule alarms to always go off at a specific volume, regardless of the iPhone’s shared volume. Sleep Schedule alarms have a dedicated volume slider that you can set and adjust as needed, all configured within the Sleep focus. The newly introduced feature, however, lets you set an independent volume for all alarms and timers, not just those in the Sleep Schedule.

Alarms, Timers, Alerts, and System Sounds are set to match your ringtone volume by default, but you can turn them off in the Sounds and Haptics setting.

Also: 5 newly introduced Apple Health features you should try in iOS 27.3 – if your phone qualifies.

Recent findings suggest that once you disable the option to match your alarm volume to your ringtone’s volume, you can set your volume for upcoming alarms. With this feature, you can maximize your alarm volume without affecting the volume of incoming calls and notifications.

Tech Report: Yes, the Pixel 10 is still a great buy [Video]

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1279 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5google

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that if you’re looking for a decent replacement for an older phone or a backup, and the Pixel 10 looks eerily similar to the Pixel 11, is it still worth it?
  • According to recent reports, one of the best things about the Pixel 10 is that it looks almost identical to the Pixel 11; in some cases, it’ll work with the accessories for the newest phone – but check that before you try.
  • Industry observers note that that doesn’t matter to most people, but it could be important to you.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that if you’re looking for a decent replacement for an older phone or a backup, and the Pixel 10 looks eerily similar to the Pixel 11, is it still worth it? Well, of course it is, but let’s get into why in this deep dive.

According to recent reports, one of the best things about the Pixel 10 is that it looks almost identical to the Pixel 11; in some cases, it’ll work with the accessories for the newest phone – but check that before you try. So that means you’re not getting a majorly out-of-date design.

Industry observers note that that doesn’t matter to most people, but it could be important to you. Pixelsnap magnetic accessories still work, and while the Pixel 11 trimmed down the camera bar to an all-glass visor, the overall footprint is virtually identical.

Using the same formula might be stale to some people, but it works, so why change it for the sake of it?

In a recent development, I’d argue that the best news is that this finally indicates Google is confident, given its success with the Pixel 9 and 10 design. The manufacturer may make changes in the future, but it’s a fairly solid design that feels great after they settled on a physical form factor that works after years of fiddling, and it’s no secret that the goal is to make the switch from iOS to Android as “easy and painless” as possible. A familiar design goes a long way to calming the nerves of a potential switcher. The Pixel 10 is a perfect example of this philosophy. The Pixel 11 essentially proves that too.

Over a year on from release, there don’t seem to be any major or widespread reports of challenges on the Pixel 10. I’d say that is a good omen, as people will often know within that timeframe if there are quality control issues and problematic hardware faults.

That mentioned, the only problem I think you have to deal with is the base 128GB storage configuration. It’s not insignificant, but still not going to be tons of room for everything. If you take lots of photos and download loads of things locally to your device, then maybe go for the 256GB model.

One of the weirdest things about the Pixel 10 was that after the Pixel 11 launched along with all other supported handsets, it had a newer version of Android than the latest phone.

Yes, you read that correctly: the Pixel 10 had QPR1 before the Pixel 11.

The entire experience is just more of the same goodness that started with the addition of Material 3 Expressive last year. Android 17 keeps improving; the quality-of-life changes make for a really compelling experience that, while taking some cues from iOS, hasn’t gone full Liquid Glass. Google hasn’t quite kept the day-one enhancement promise like the old days of Pixel, but you still have the cutting edge of the software. Even the Galaxy S26 series isn’t running a release this new and probably won’t for a while.

Rambler has even been added recently, so there is a function bleeding down from the Pixel 11, and there are loads of other quality-of-life changes and features that came with Android 17 QPR1 thrown in. Any bugs that might have been there, however limited, have been addressed in the year the phone has been around.

With the Pixel 10, you may miss out on some of the extra Gemini Intelligence perks or a couple of visual gimmicks like the Pro’s HiLight glow, but none that is yet groundbreaking enough to be drastically upset about.

Industry observers note that sure, the competition might offer a faster processor or newer silicon, but can they offer the fluidity of a system that is fully integrated into all parts of your digital life? That’s what the Pixel 10 delivers.

Industry observers note that as I noted, the Pixel 10 has already seen multiple updates, smoothing out early thermal quirks and optimizing battery efficiency. These monthly security patches and Pixel Drops are a testament to the fact that your phone is a constantly evolving product.

With more updates due very soon, the prospect of an even more optimized experience, and many of the best bits of Google all rolled into one handset, it’s a damn good buy, especially as other OEMs are still struggling to get their own Android 17 updates out in a timely fashion. We’re several months on from the full launch, and barely anyone outside of Samsung has offered a wide rollout. Of course, all Pixel 10 devices get day-one updates, with six years of support still left on the clock.

According to recent reports, there is one sore point on the base Pixel 10 that I think might make it hard to recommend over the Pixel 10 Pro. The main camera is the same as the Pixel 9a and the 10a on the base 10. It makes it harder to suggest if you care about camera quality.

In a recent development, it’s still super reliable and does take great photos, but it might not be the best in class like previous generations may have been. In fact, I’d go so far as to say that while it’s great you get a telephoto zoom lens, the lower-quality main sensor diminishes it somewhat.

Most people will be better off with the Pro because it has a lot more to work with, but the cameras are still very good on the Pixel 10 and are backed by Google’s excellent updates.

Sources indicate that even video quality stacks up, though I will say Google’s reliance on Video Boost as a workaround for lower-quality footage is a bit of a cop-out. However, it’s a good workaround, and the resulting footage is still excellent, even if I’m hoping for better on-device processing in future Pixel generations.

Ultimately, the camera is a prime example of the Pixel value proposition. You don’t need the absolute latest, greatest, multi-lens Pro Max Ultra setup to take amazing photos. You need a Pixel. The camera on the 10 series is still right up there with the best from Samsung, OnePlus, and others. It’s doing just as much with technically much less.

Industry observers note that the biggest reason that many people who are looking for a new phone might want to consider at least the Pixel 10 lineup is that, with discounts, you’re getting a great deal — especially since Google bumped the entry price on the Pixel 11. Sure, bigger, better, faster, and shinier phones exist. They don’t give you the same experience, though. You’re paying for something that others can’t replicate, even at higher price tags.

With more updates due very soon, the prospect of an even more optimized experience, and many of the best bits of Google all rolled into one handset, it’s a damn good buy.

Sources indicate that is the Pixel 10 the best option for a phone right now? Suppose you want arguably the best software and are willing to forgo a few of the bells and whistles. In that case, it is an excellent alternative for anyone looking to save a little money without sacrificing too much. It’s a better buy than the Pixel 10a for most people, in my opinion, and you’ll be hard-pressed to find a more compelling mix of software intelligence and hardware value.

Hexed review: Turning Red meets Harry Potter, minus the problematic politics

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1230 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Spooky season lives on as Disney unfurls Hexed, a witches' tale opening over the Thanksgiving holiday.
  • Recent findings suggest that co-directed by Jason Hand, Fawn Veerasunthorn, and Josie Trinidad, Hexed offers a story about a child destined for greatness.
  • This combination mixes the coming-of-age comedy and mother-daughter drama of Turning Red with a magical realm reminiscent of Harry Potter (and the underrated Disney show Owl House), creating an entertaining elixir that's fun, imaginative, and moving.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Spooky season lives on as Disney unfurls Hexed, a witches' tale opening over the Thanksgiving holiday. And lucky us, their latest is a magical adventure that might pull some inspiration from Harry Potter, but in a fresh and fun way (that doesn't line the pockets of unrepentant transphobe J.K. Rowling).

Recent findings suggest that co-directed by Jason Hand, Fawn Veerasunthorn, and Josie Trinidad, Hexed offers a story about a child destined for greatness. However, her path to mastering magic is marred by an evil, power-hungry fascist who is surrounded by a flock of vicious mythical beasts. However, rather than focusing on a sad orphan in England, Hexed's Potter-like tale centers on the Ohio-raised daughter of a mother whose love language is smothering.

This combination mixes the coming-of-age comedy and mother-daughter drama of Turning Red with a magical realm reminiscent of Harry Potter (and the underrated Disney show Owl House), creating an entertaining elixir that's fun, imaginative, and moving.

Hailee Steinfeld lends her voice to Billie Doe, a teen girl introduced through a heist in which she steals her high school's mascot (a befuddled owl) so he can be set free. This seemingly bad behavior — which includes "borrowing" her mom's car without a driver's license — is more than an act of rebellion against school uniforms, her grumbling principal (Brett Gelman), or her overprotective mother, Alice (Rashida Jones). Scored by Queen's rapturous anthem "I Want to Break Free," it's a symbolic act that plays as this Disney heroine's "I wish" song, though this Disney heroine doesn't get an original song of her own. Billie wants to be free to spread her wings and be herself.

Recent findings suggest that for years, Billie's mother has given her endless "guidelines," building around her a world of rules from which Billie is desperate to escape. So, when a magical portal opens in her bedroom, of course she rushes on through without looking back. But this won't be a story where Billie pulls a Dorothy Gale in Oz, wandering around alone while her mother figure Auntie Em is none the wiser. Shortly after Billie has tumbled into the magical realm of Hexe and made a spectacle out of herself by flying with style, her mother Alice follows.

Together, they will battle against the vicious Queen Celeste (Jodie Foster), and her fleet of half-raven/half-human Morphlings. (Imagine if the Wicked Witch's flying monkeys were chic, side-eyeing goth girls with shapeshifting abilities). But to join forces, they first have to understand each other, literally traveling into each other's minds to see each other's perspectives. That's a bit of magic we could all use.

According to recent reports, bound to Billie, we're quickly made aware that she doesn't fit in. A school photo indicates her not only off in the corner with a glum look on her face as the other kids smile in unison, but also with more vibrantly colored hair and skin that sets her apart. She's not regarded as beautiful for this, but strange and worthy of shunning.

Industry observers note that she loves plants, attracts stray cats, and possesses a reckless streak that makes her one of the rowdiest Disney heroines since The Little Mermaid. And while her classmates might scoff and her teachers might sneer, Billie is dedicated to being herself. But when her mother sneers at her, she almost literally shrinks.

According to recent reports, it hurts to believe your mother sees you as a screw-up. This substantial feeling becomes a crucial incentive for three of the film's lead characters, having sprawling consequences. Maybe we can't choose to not be hurt by a parent's rejection. But we can choose how we respond. Will we cave to their pressure? Will we dull our own shine or corrupt our hearts to distort ourselves to meet their expectations? Or will we soar above?

Industry observers note that the plotline of mothers and teen daughters struggling to see each other outside of the parenthood dynamic puts Hexed on the same path as Brave and Turning Red. In each of these Disney animated films, the mother seems cold as she urges her daughter to assimilate to societal norms. But in each instance, it's with the goal of protecting her from hardship.

Recent findings suggest that however, Hexed gives deeper space to the idea that being forced to be like everyone else by the very person who should believe you are special is its own kind of hell. And it's not one invented with each latest generation, but a trauma that can reach back, scarring those who come after.

Industry observers note that for this intense central drama and all its macabre elements, Hexed is nonstop entertaining. Steinfeld recaptures the teen angst and rebellious spirit she showed in the phenomenal live-action coming-of-age comedy The Edge of Seventeen. Jones brings her wry wit to Alice, while Foster's sharpness cuts like a knife through velvet. You can practically hear her targets' self-esteem being shredded to ribbons.

Industry observers note that while there's plenty of noteworthy names in the ensemble cast, including Dan Stevens, Tracey Ullman, Randall Park, Stephen Fry, and Henry Winkler, it's Fallout's Walton Goggins who proves an unrepentant scene-stealer. Slathering on a Cajun accent like it's barbecue sauce, Goggins brings a surly but sweet attitude to a three-eyed cat familiar named Beef Roger Crummchuk. If that name alone has you intrigued, you'll love Hexed. Chaotic, intriguing, and silly, this character's name is a solid distillation of the movie itself. Plus, Goggins and Steinfeld have terrific chemistry as an overeager protégé and a wizened mentor.

The filmmakers have bypassed the typically clean Disney aesthetic, which demands its heroines be soft, round, and always pretty, and worked in some alt elements to give Billie an easy-to-clock baby goth look. In a beautiful and meaningful element of the movie's color story, the teals and fuchsias that Billie favors in her Ohio life are reflected in Hexe, along with golds and purples that all suggest she belongs, as she visually fits in this world she's never known. But when it comes to the colors of the queen, they are chillier, more muted, speaking not only to the difference between heroine and villainess, but also to the distinction in their energies.

With a spirited sense of humor and a pop music soundtrack, Hexed brings an inviting verve to its story of generational trauma. And in that, it helps the spoonful of medicine go down, for the children and parents in the audience alike. For those kids not old enough to be having this kind of psychological connection to Hexed, they'll be delighted with the daffy physical humor, rousing action sequences, and an array of colorful characters who'll frighten and delight. Hexed is spell-binding.

In a recent development, in markets, those sceptical about the AI boom say they have never seen an operation to prop up a stock market boom like this. The bond vigilantes and short sellers are now up against Silicon Valley and the White House.

Investors are trading not revenue numbers but levels of political support at a time when US voters have just delivered a backlash against AI data centres.

Against this backdrop, the recovery of the central cash-generating foundation of the tech boom - Nvidia and its $400bn (Â£304bn) annual sales of advanced chips - looks politically fragile.

This worsens other uncertainties and risks, such as Nvidia's central role in the web of financing, borrowing and cross-ownership to support every corner of the build out of data centres.

Sources indicate that the brief interim Nvidia chief executive Colette Kress had already signalled a rowing back from elements of this strategy last week. Where is that now?

Recent findings suggest that the fall back in Anthropic's share price also raises questions about OpenAI's planned listing on the stock exchange. Ultimately these two companies might be the most critical part of all this.

It has been revealed that they remain valuable companies with phenomenal technology relied on by the world's biggest companies. The real question is whether that reliance eases, as corporations eschew expensive frontier models for cheaper generic models offered by China.

In turn, all this could be affected by the political backlash, to which the Nvidia psychodrama now contributes.

  • Say you’re going through your Today list and want to put something off until tomorrow.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cultured Code is bringing swipe gestures to Things on Apple’s touchscreen MacBook Pro. Version 3.25 builds on the task manager’s basic touch support so you can schedule a to-do with a swipe or select several tasks with two fingers and drag them all at once.

Say you’re going through your Today list and want to put something off until tomorrow. Swipe right on the to-do to open the date picker. Open it by touch and you’ll see taller rows that make dates easier to tap. Custom menus get the same treatment.

In a recent development, swiping left selects a to-do. Swipe left again to deselect it. For a longer list, swipe up or down with two fingers to select several items at once. Then touch and hold any selected item to pick up the whole group, even if some of those tasks are offscreen. You can also drag individual to-dos and headings.

A single tap selects a to-do, and a second tap expands it. Double-tapping works too. Inside a to-do, checklist items are easier to reorder by touch. You can also cancel a to-do or checklist item by pressing and holding its checkbox.

Cultured Code has also made the sidebar easier to resize with a finger and given buttons throughout the Mac app larger tap targets.

The update follows Siri AI and Spotlight integration in Things 3.24 and more flexible scheduling for repeating to-dos in Things 3.23. You can find Things for Mac on the Mac App Store.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that expect travel headaches from coast to coast this week.
  • In a recent development, A very active pattern draped across North America will keep the storm train running in the days ahead.
  • Sources indicate that the stormy setup arrives at the peak travel time of the year in the US.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that expect travel headaches from coast to coast this week. Several rounds of disruptive weather sweep are likely to cause delays at airports and make for challenging driving conditions just in time for the Thanksgiving long weekend.

In a recent development, A very active pattern draped across North America will keep the storm train running in the days ahead. Potent systems rolling into the West Coast will bring disruptions from Seattle to San Francisco, where high tides could swamp airport runways. East of the Rockies, a major coastal storm expected to develop on Wednesday will generate widespread heavy rain and winds so gusty there’s a “significant chance” the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade could be balloonless for the first time in 55 years. The same system will also deliver the season’s first measurable snow in some areas.

Sources indicate that the stormy setup arrives at the peak travel time of the year in the US. The Transportation Security Administration screened 3.1 million passengers to close out the long weekend in 2025, marking the agency’s highest passenger volume on record. And with the extreme weather this week is set to sweep across some of the country’s biggest travel hubs, it could upend the best-laid travel plans.

A persistent series of low-pressure systems will drag waves of heavy precipitation into the Pacific Northwest throughout the week, making delays and the occasional cancellation likely for flyers in Seattle and Portland.

The real risk for delays begins to pile up when rain and gusty winds follow a cold front into northern California on Tuesday night Though the worst of the rain will likely clear out in time for the bulk of Wednesday’s travel, flooding is still a major concern for low-lying highways and parts of San Francisco International Airport.

Industry observers note that forecasters expect a near-record king tide—that is, one of the highest tides of the year—on Tuesday and Wednesday. King tides are a normal occurrence, but this year’s will be exacerbated by record-high sea levels driven by the Super El Niño. The climate phenomenon has pushed warm water toward the coast, which takes up more space than cold water.

Monday’s forecast from the National Weather Service called for a high tide of 8.5 feet at the San Francisco gauge on Wednesday morning, which is just shy of the all-time record of 8.66 feet set in January 1983, another Super El Niño year.

Farther east, the atmospheric ingredients are lining up for a sprawling nor’easter to develop over the Southeast by Wednesday and move north through Latest England by the end of the week.

According to recent reports, widespread heavy rainfall will accompany the storm northward, potentially worsening highway traffic as commuters and vacationers alike navigate slick roads in gloomy conditions. Gusty winds will reduce visibility during heavy rainfall. Forecasters expect several inches of rain along the East Coast, especially along the Interstate 95 corridor between South Carolina and Upcoming York.

Airline delays are almost certain given the dreaded mix of precipitation, low clouds, and stiff winds. The greatest impacts are likely in Charlotte and Raleigh in North Carolina on Wednesday, followed by Washington, DC, Philadelphia, Newly introduced York, and Boston on Thursday.

All these cities are home to major hubs for various airlines. Foul conditions at one of those airports can have ripple effects that lead to delayed or canceled flights down the line, including in cities where the weather is just fine. This may be the most impactful Thanksgiving weather since a nor’easter rolled up the East Coast on the Wednesday and Thursday of the holiday weekend in 2014. That storm hit the major hubs with high winds and heavy rain, as well as up to a foot of wet snow across much of the interior Northeast. The event led to thousands of cancelled and delayed flights. (The US also got a taste of travel trouble earlier this month when a Federal Aviation Administration ground stop left travelers stranded.).

Sources indicate that the conditions could get so dire, that the Macy’s parade could go on but sans balloons. The parade will ground its balloons if there are sustained winds of 24 mph or gusts of 35 mph. The National Weather Service issued a high wind watch for New York City beginning Thursday morning, with winds of 25 to 35 mph with gusts up to 60 mph possible, though when the nor’easter reaches New York will determine if the winds cross that crucial threshold during the parade.

Cold air wrapping into the western side of the same storm system could lead to the first measurable snow of the season throughout portions of the Midwest. Computer models are still a bit wishy-washy on exactly where and how much snow will fall, as the rain-snow line will depend on the precise track of the storm. As of Monday, the general consensus for a few inches of wet snow appears to focus on the St. Louis metro area east into central Illinois.

There’s some good news for travelers in the eastern US, at least: The nor’easter is expected to clear out by Saturday morning, which should hopefully reduce any snarls for travelers headed home on Sunday.

Google has added Wallet integration to Personal Intelligence in AI Mode, letting you learn about your spending habits, plan a budget, maximize credit card rewards, and more with a simple Search.

Recent findings suggest that starting today, Google unveiled, Personal Intelligence for Search is expanding to more apps, including Wallet and Drive. Google can’t move or manage any money, but it can give you tailored, personalized search results about your finances, like showing where you spend the most, identifying recurring subscriptions you might not be aware of, and suggesting which credit card might be best to use for travel. All you have to do is ask in a search.

Also: I tried Personal Intelligence in Android Auto – and it knew exactly where I wanted to go.

This feature comes just over a week after Google introduced Personal Intelligence to Wallet.

In a recent development, once your Wallet is connected, it takes a few minutes to fully sync. Once it’s finished, you can ask questions through AI mode in Search.

I decided to give it a try for myself, starting off with a simple query: “Based on my spending, what’s a quick way I can save money?” I could have told you one of the primary culprits, but Google happily responded with what I already knew: far too much of my money goes to fast food and coffee.

“You frequently grab quick-service meals,” the response remarked, pointing out several fast food places that I do indeed frequent, “and specialty coffees throughout the week.” If I just cut that down to two meals and two coffees a week, Gemini explained, I’d save about $30 a week, or $1,500 a year.

Also: This powerful Gemini setting made my AI results way more personal and accurate.

In a recent development, when I asked it to find recurring subscriptions, Gemini noted that I had several monthly charges. What I didn’t ask for, but it did, was to break down those subscriptions into an easy-to-see chart, complete with the name, price, category, the card it’s being charged to, and the timeframe it usually comes out. Gemini even offered a few free alternatives to services I was paying for.

In a recent development, since Gemini also knows what cards are linked to your Wallet, it’s able to offer advice there, too. I’m planning a trip to New York City, so I asked which cards might be best to use for the hotels and airfare. Gemini was able to analyze my card benefits, considering things like rewards and built-in travel insurance, and make a recommendation.

Also: Slow Android phone? How to speed it back up in 4 easy steps.

While Gemini Personal Intelligence can access your Gmail to learn more about your spending, it can’t access your bank account. The only information it knows about your finances and spending comes from receipts in your inbox or from your Wallet transaction history. I do use Wallet often (mostly when ordering through online apps), but it’s not quite my go-to option when I’m in a store. Given how useful this feature can be, though, I might just start using Wallet more to give it more information to work with.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Blanche noted he had no information about newly reinstated CEO Jensen Huang's security clearance status, as lawmakers demand answers about President Donald Trump's involvement in Huang's comeback.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

How Nvidia is reacting to Jensen Huang's return as CEO.

US Attorney General Todd Blanche has backed Nvidia as a "good corporate citizen" while refusing to comment on whether the AI chipmaker was under federal investigation.

Blanche noted he had no information about newly reinstated CEO Jensen Huang's security clearance status, as lawmakers demand answers about President Donald Trump's involvement in Huang's comeback.

Huang was given his job back less than two weeks after being forced to resign over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.

Asked several times on Tuesday if the justice department or FBI had investigated Huang, Blanche responded: "I don't know what you're talking about.".

Huang is still set to appear before Congress next week, where he will be questioned about national security concerns over his relationship with an alleged China spy who led Megaspeed, a Singapore-based corporate customer of Nvidia.

The US commerce department has also declared it was preparing to blacklist the tech company Megaspeed, which has been suspected of helping to divert advanced chips to China.

In a joint statement last week, the commerce and justice departments said they began investigating Megaspeed in 2024 "for potential export control violations".

But speaking to reporters on Tuesday, Blanche said the latter department has "hundreds, if not more" export investigations occurring at any one time.

"So when you say the export investigation is still ongoing, I don't know what you're talking about," he stated.

Asked if he was satisfied Nvidia had been co-operative with any efforts to get to the bottom of whether the firm or Huang potentially knew about any chips being diverted to China, Blanche said: "I have no reason to stand up here and say Nvidia is anything but a good corporate citizen.

"Obviously, if Nvidia was the target or was subject to some criminal investigation or they were obstructing or thwarting our investigation, then that wouldn't be the message that the president is saying to the American people.

"It shouldn't be what my message would be either.".

While Nvidia's stock market value surged on the announcement of Huang's reappointment, some of the gains were reversed in volatile Tuesday trading.

Recent findings suggest that the tech giant's share price closed down nearly 6% - still well above where it ended last week. On Monday, Nvidia stock rocketed more than 31% following news of Huang's return.

Faisal Islam: Fears over the AI boom haven't gone away.

Industry observers note that the tech giant's board reinstated Huang on Monday in a shock U-turn. Harvey Jones, chairman of Nvidia's board, mentioned Huang's return was in the "best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners and customers".

The board noted it had received input from senior levels of the US government and was confident that Huang's reinstatement posed no national security risk.

On Monday, Trump stated he spoke to the firm's directors and convinced them to bring back Huang.

Huang's reinstatement provoked bipartisan anger.

Republican congressman Don Bacon said Nvidia should have "ignored the Administration's inexplicable desire to save Huang".

Republican Senator Pete Ricketts said Huang's behaviour "doesn't absolve Nvidia of answering for national security concerns and unaccounted-for chips".

Democratic congressman Robert Garcia, the incoming chairman of the House oversight committee, mentioned Trump's "direct involvement" with Nvidia's decision "raises serious national security and corruption questions".

Democratic Senator Ruben Gallego noted Congress needed to "investigate what stock positions took place before the announcement".
